cards.front: Recall a key point about Comparing & Evaluating Dance
cards.back: Comparing requires identifying both similarities and differences — not just one or the other

cards.front: Recall a key point about Comparing & Evaluating Dance
cards.back: Use linking words: 'similarly', 'in contrast', 'whereas', 'both', 'however' to show comparison clearly

cards.front: Recall a key point about Comparing & Evaluating Dance
cards.back: Always compare the same element — for example, compare use of dynamics in both works

cards.front: Recall a key point about Comparing & Evaluating Dance
cards.back: Evaluating means making a judgement about effectiveness, supported by specific evidence

cards.front: Recall a key point about Comparing & Evaluating Dance
cards.back: A strong evaluation considers strengths and limitations before reaching a conclusion

cards.front: Recall a key point about Comparing & Evaluating Dance
cards.back: When evaluating your own work, be honest and specific about what worked and what could improve

cards.front: Recall a key point about Comparing & Evaluating Dance
cards.back: Use criteria for evaluation: intention, audience impact, technical execution, choreographic structure

cards.front: Recall a key point about Comparing & Evaluating Dance
cards.back: Comparison questions may ask about two professional works or your work versus a professional work

cards.front: Recall a key point about Comparing & Evaluating Dance
cards.back: Always reference specific moments or sections from the works you are comparing

cards.front: Recall a key point about Comparing & Evaluating Dance
cards.back: Evaluation answers should end with a clear, stated judgement, not just a list of points

cards.front: Recall a key point about Comparing & Evaluating Dance
cards.back: Avoid vague statements like 'they are different' — state exactly how and why

cards.front: Recall a key point about Comparing & Evaluating Dance
cards.back: AQA 8236 assessment rewards depth of analysis over breadth of coverage
